sentences.text: Being dissatisfied with the award of compensation of Rs.1,92,000/-, the claimant is in this appeal seeking enhancement.
2. The occurrence of the accident and the liability to pay compensation by the KSRTC are not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 12% by taking into consideration the medical evidence of the doctor, who had not treated the claimant that he had suffered the disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.
In my view, this assessment of disability cannot be found fault with.
4. The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant as Rs.7,000/-, since there was no evidence to that effect.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.9,000/- for the accident of the year 2015, it would NC: 2024:KHC:50783 be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/-.
5. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,78,200/- (Rs.9,000/- X 12 X '11' X 15%) towards loss of future earnings.
6. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.10,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the said sum to Rs.75,000/- and Rs.50,000/- respectively under the said heads.

7. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.6,000/-
towards 'medical expenses', the same is just and proper and is accordingly affirmed.
8. A sum of Rs.15,000/- has been awarded towards 'conveyance, food nourishment and attendant charges'.
Since the claimant has been hospitalised for 13 days, it would be appropriate to award Rs.20,000/- under the said head.
